Bali, Indonesia: Terraced rice fields, temple-dotted coastline and surf breaks, all on one island.
Tokyo, Japan: One of the world's largest cities, known for its food, rail network and mix of old shrines and neon districts.
Cape Town, South Africa: A harbor city under Table Mountain, minutes from beaches, vineyards and the Cape Peninsula.
Sydney, Australia: Harbour, Opera House and beaches within easy reach of the city center.
Maldives (Male): Low-lying coral atolls in the Indian Ocean, famous for lagoons and overwater resorts.
Buenos Aires, Argentina: A walkable capital known for tango, steakhouses and European-style architecture.
Rio de Janeiro, Brazil: Beaches and granite peaks in the same skyline, with Christ the Redeemer above it all.
Phuket, Thailand: Thailand's largest island, with beaches on the Andaman Sea and easy boat trips to nearby islands.
Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam: Vietnam's biggest city, packed with street food, markets and French-colonial landmarks.
Taipei, Taiwan: Night markets, hot springs and mountain trails, all reachable by the city's metro.
Amalfi Coast, Italy: Cliffside villages and lemon terraces stacked above the Tyrrhenian Sea.
Algarve, Portugal: Southern Portugal's coast of golden cliffs, sea caves and sheltered beaches.
Athens, Greece: The Acropolis and Parthenon sit over a busy city of tavernas and neighborhood cafes.
Thessaloniki, Greece: A waterfront city in northern Greece with Byzantine churches and a strong food scene.
Larnaca, Cyprus: A Mediterranean seafront town with a palm-lined promenade and a well-known salt lake.
Madrid, Spain: Spain's capital, home to the Prado museum, late dinners and big central parks.
Dubrovnik, Croatia: A walled medieval old town on the Adriatic that you can circle on foot along the ramparts.
Tulum, Mexico: Mayan ruins perched over the Caribbean, with cenotes and beaches nearby.
Mallorca, Spain: Balearic island with coves, mountain villages and a cathedral-topped capital, Palma.
San Jose, Costa Rica: The gateway to Costa Rica's volcanoes, cloud forests and both coasts.
Da Nang, Vietnam: A beach city in central Vietnam, close to Hoi An's old town and the Marble Mountains.
Cebu, Philippines: A gateway to island-hopping, waterfalls and whale-shark and sardine-run diving spots.
Prague, Czechia: Well-preserved medieval center, a castle above the river and a strong beer tradition.
Budapest, Hungary: Two cities on either side of the Danube, known for thermal baths and grand riverside architecture.
Sofia / Borovets, Bulgaria: A low-key capital with easy access to Bulgaria's largest ski resort, Borovets.
Bogota, Colombia: A high-altitude capital with museums, street art and coffee culture.
Krakow, Poland: A largely intact medieval old town and a historic Jewish quarter, Kazimierz.
Bucharest, Romania: Romania's capital, with the enormous Palace of the Parliament and a busy old-town nightlife scene.
Guatemala City, Guatemala: The main entry point for Guatemala's highlands, Maya sites and colonial towns.
Marrakech, Morocco: A walled medina, souks and riads, with the Atlas Mountains on the horizon.
Cappadocia, Turkey: Volcanic rock formations and cave dwellings, famous for sunrise hot-air balloon rides.
Petra, Jordan: An ancient city carved into rose-colored sandstone, reached through a narrow canyon.
Oaxaca, Mexico: Known for mole, mezcal and markets, with Zapotec ruins nearby.
Cusco, Peru: The old Inca capital and the usual starting point for Machu Picchu and the Sacred Valley.
Luxor, Egypt: Home to the Valley of the Kings and Karnak Temple on the banks of the Nile.
Tbilisi, Georgia: A hillside old town with sulfur baths, wine culture and Georgian cuisine.
Baku, Azerbaijan: A Caspian Sea port with a walled old city beside modern glass towers.
Antigua, Guatemala: A colonial town ringed by volcanoes, with cobblestone streets and ruined churches.
Muscat, Oman: A coastal capital of forts, souks and rugged mountains, known for a relaxed pace.
Lisbon, Portugal: Hilltop neighborhoods, trams, custard tarts and views over the Tagus River.
